Furthermore, by means of the analytical knowledge of phenomena (*dharma-pratisaṃvid*), one knows that all Buddhas attain perfect enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*) in a single instant;
by means of the analytical knowledge of meaning (*artha-pratisaṃvid*), one knows the distinctions between the various characteristics of events and times.
By means of the analytical knowledge of language, they expound the Dharma by providing detailed explanations according to their perfect realization;
by means of the analytical knowledge of eloquence, they explain each and every phrase of the Dharma inexhaustibly throughout immeasurable eons.

"Furthermore, by means of the analytical knowledge of phenomena (*dharmapratisaṃvid*), one knows the power of the Buddhas' speech, their fearlessnesses, their unique Buddha-qualities (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*), their great loving-kindness and great compassion, their eloquence and application, their turning of the great wheel of Dharma, and their practice in accordance with the wisdom of all-knowledge.

By means of the analytical knowledge of meaning (*arthapratisaṃvid*), one thoroughly understands how the Tathāgata, according to the eighty-four thousand different types of conduct among sentient beings, utters sounds and words in accordance with their inclinations, faculties, and resolutions.

By means of the analytical knowledge of expression (*niruktipratisaṃvid*), one expounds the True Dharma for sentient beings using the Buddha's voice and words in accordance with their diverse modes of conduct."

By means of the unimpeded analytical knowledge of eloquence (*pratibhāna-pratisaṃvid*), they expound the Dharma with a resolute conviction (*adhimukti*) that accords with the wheel of pure conduct of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.
"O Son of the Buddha!

Having dwelt in the ninth stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*), the Bodhisattva accomplishes such unimpeded analytical knowledge and wisdom; they obtain the treasury of the Buddha-dharma and become a great Dharma-preacher."

They attain the dhāraṇī of possessing complete meaning, the dhāraṇī of possessing the Dharma, the dhāraṇī of possessing the wisdom of elicitation, the dhāraṇī of possessing radiant illumination, the dhāraṇī of possessing excellent wisdom, the dhāraṇī of possessing manifold wealth, the dhāraṇī of possessing majestic power, the dhāraṇī of possessing unimpeded gates, the dhāraṇī of possessing boundless limits, and the dhāraṇī of possessing various meanings; they thus obtain a full million *asaṃkhyeya* such dhāraṇīs, and by means of a million *asaṃkhyeya* skillful vocal elements and various doors of immeasurable eloquence, they expound the Dharma for others.

By means of such immeasurable hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* dharanī-gates, this bodhisattva hears the sublime Dharma from immeasurable Buddhas; having heard it, they do not forget it, and they are able to expound the heard Dharma with immeasurable distinctions. Before a single Buddha, they receive the true Dharma through ten million *asaṃkhyeya* dharanī-gates; as it is before one Buddha, so it is likewise before immeasurable Buddhas.

Yet, in a single moment of thought, this bodhisattva receives immeasurable gateways of sublime Dharma before the Buddha, the World-Honored One, the Perfectly Awakened One; such extensive learning he attains that even a śrāvaka who upholds what he has heard could not receive it in hundreds of thousands of kalpas.

Having thus accomplished these various dhāraṇīs and attained eloquence, this bodhisattva sits upon the Dharma throne and pervades the trichiliocosm, preaching the Dharma according to the diverse inclinations of sentient beings.

That Dharma-seat is most preeminent; except for the Buddhas and those Bodhisattvas of the highest stages who have received empowerment, no other Bodhisattvas possess the majestic power and radiance that can compare to it.

And this bodhisattva, seated upon the Dharma throne, because he acts according to his own inclination, expounds the sublime Dharma with a single voice and terminology, enabling the entire great assembly to understand it completely.
Or, according to their own wishes, they may analyze [the teachings] through various words and vocal expressions, causing the entire great assembly to attain awakening.
Or, according to their own wishes, they may emit great radiance, from which they manifest immeasurable Dharma gates.
Or, according to their own wish, they cause the sound of the Dharma to issue forth from every single pore of their bodies.
Or, according to their own wish, from all the forms and images manifested within this trichiliocosm, they are able to produce the sublime sounds of the wondrous Dharma.
Or, according to their own wish, they may, with a single sound or word, universally manifest the sounds of all dharmas.
Or, according to their own wish, they may empower all existing sounds and words so that they all become the subtle and wondrous sound of the Dharma.
Or, according to their own wish, they cause all the sounds of songs and music belonging to every world to proclaim the voice of the Dharma.
Or, according to their own wish, they produce from the sound of a single syllable the distinct sounds of all phenomena.

Or, according to their own wishes, they cause every single atom within the aggregates of the four great elements—earth, water, fire, and wind—in unspeakably infinite worlds to all produce unspeakable Dharma-gates.

Suppose that all sentient beings bound within a thousandfold world-system were to come before him, and in a single kṣaṇa, muhūrta, or instant, each were to pose questions and challenges using immeasurable voices and sounds, with each question being distinct from the others; yet this Bodhisattva, in the span of a single thought-moment, is able to receive and comprehend every one of those voices, word by word and phrase by phrase, and then provide explanations for them all with a single voice, causing each person to find joy according to their own inclinations.

Suppose that in two thousand or three thousand worlds, or even throughout unspeakably many trichiliocosms, every sentient being therein were to pose difficult questions using immeasurable voices and sounds, each question being distinct from the others, and all of them were to do so in a single instant; the Bodhisattva would be able to receive and comprehend them all within a single thought-moment, and would likewise provide explanations for them all with a single voice, causing each to find joy according to their own inclinations.

Extending even to unspeakably, unspeakably many worlds, he expounds the sublime Dharma according to the inclinations, faculties, and understandings of sentient beings; having attained the discourse on the Dharma and sought the empowerment of the Buddhas, he is able to turn the wheel of Dharma and extensively perform the Buddha-work, universally serving as a refuge for all sentient beings.
"Furthermore, this bodhisattva further upholds such illumination of the Dharma and makes this vow:

'Suppose that upon the tip of a single hair there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many worlds, each preaching the Dharma to various assemblies; and each Tathāgata likewise preaches the Dharma to various sentient beings according to their differences in mental disposition, bestowing unspeakably many immeasurable Dharma-gates upon each individual being's inclinations;
as it is within the assembly of one Tathāgata, so it is within the assemblies of all Tathāgatas.'"

Just as it is at the tip of a single hair, so it is throughout the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); within this, we should generate such immeasurable power of mindfulness that we may receive all the illuminations of the Dharma from all the Tathāgatas.

When a Bodhisattva dwells in this Stage of Excellent Intelligence (Sādhumatī), day and night they increasingly cultivate no other mental attention, entering the realm of the Buddhas, drawing near to the Tathāgatas, and attaining the profound liberation of a Bodhisattva.
Following such wisdom, this bodhisattva remains constantly in meditative absorption, directly beholding all Buddhas without ever for a moment ceasing;

within each eon, they behold immeasurable Buddhas, immeasurable hundreds of Buddhas, immeasurable thousands of Buddhas, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of Buddhas, immeasurable koṭis of Buddhas, immeasurable hundreds of koṭis of Buddhas, immeasurable thousands of koṭis of Buddhas, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Buddhas, and even immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭi-nayutas of Buddhas.

Constantly making offerings and serving with subtle and exquisite articles of worship, they pose various questions to the Buddhas; having attained the dhāraṇīs of the Dharma, they are further able to expound them. Thus, these roots of goodness of the bodhisattvas become increasingly bright and pure, such that they cannot be eclipsed by anything else.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like a skilled goldsmith who, having refined gold, fashions it into an ornamental object and polishes it until it is perfectly finished.
A universal monarch (cakravartin) then uses it to adorn his head, or places it around his neck.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha! Among all the minor regional kings and all the subjects and citizens within the four continents, there were none whose ornaments could equal his.

When a bodhisattva dwells in this stage of Excellent Intelligence (sādhumatī), these roots of goodness are likewise such that they cannot be equaled by any śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or any bodhisattvas dwelling in the lower stages.

Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha! The light of these roots of goodness of the Bodhisattva is able to illuminate the dense forests of the afflictions and minds of sentient beings, causing them to turn away from them.
For example, when the Great Brahmā King, Lord of the Two-Thousandfold World System, emits light from his body, it is able to illuminate the dense forests and deep recesses throughout that system;

likewise, when a Bodhisattva dwells in this Stage of Good Intelligence (*sādhumatī*), the radiance of their roots of goodness likewise illuminates the minds and the dense forests of afflictions of sentient beings, and then returns from there.

Among the ten perfections (*pāramitā*), he has reached the further shore through the perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*) as his predominant practice; as for the remaining perfections, he practices them according to his strength and capacity, though not without cultivation.
“O Son of the Buddha!

This is called a brief explanation of the ninth stage of the bodhisattva, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*). Were it to be explained in detail, it could not be exhausted even in the course of immeasurable eons.”

The Bodhisattvas on this stage, upon taking birth, mostly become Great Brahmā Kings; possessing great majesty, they rule over two thousand world-systems. They are most preeminent and cannot be eclipsed by others; they clearly perceive what is beneficial and attain great sovereignty. They are able to expound for sentient beings the practices of the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and the Pāramitās of the Bodhisattvas. In matters of answering questions according to the inclinations of sentient beings, there is no one capable of defeating them.

Whatever deeds they perform—whether through generosity, or kind speech, or beneficial conduct, or cooperation—all of these are never apart from the mental engagement with the Buddha, the mental engagement with the Dharma, the mental engagement with the Saṅgha, the mental engagement with Bodhisattvas, the mental engagement with the Bodhisattva practices, the mental engagement with the perfections (pāramitās), the mental engagement with the stages (bhūmis), the mental engagement with the powers of a Buddha, the mental engagement with the fearlessnesses, and the mental engagement with the unique qualities of a Buddha; indeed, they are never apart from the mental engagement with the omniscient wisdom that is perfectly associated with all supreme and sublime aspects of practice.
He constantly makes this aspiration, saying:

"Among all sentient beings, I shall become the foremost, the most excellent, the most distinguished, the sublime, the most subtle, the superior, the unsurpassed, the guide, the leader, and the commander; even unto attaining the state that serves as the basis for the knowledge of all-knowledge."
If one delights in initiating such diligence, by means of this diligence, in a single kṣaṇa, muhūrta, or moment,
one attains as many samādhis as there are atoms in ten million asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields,
and is able to see as many Buddhas as there are atoms in ten million asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields, sustained by the empowerment of those Buddhas.
They are all able to comprehend and understand; they are able to shake as many worlds as there are atoms in a million *asaṃkhyeya* Buddha-fields;
they are able to travel to as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms in a million *asaṃkhyeya* Buddha-fields;
they are able to illuminate as many worlds as there are atoms in a million *asaṃkhyeya* Buddha-fields; and they are able to bring to maturity a million...
Sentient beings as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-fields, with a lifespan lasting for a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-field atoms of kalpas,
enter into a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-field atoms of kalpas each for both the past and future limits,
and contemplate and discern a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-field atoms of dharmas.
At the gate, he manifested bodies as numerous as the atoms in ten million *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-fields,
and each body was surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas equal in number to the atoms in ten million *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-fields.

From this point upward, regarding the various manifestations of play—whether of body, light, supernormal powers, eyes, spheres of activity, voice, conduct, adornments, resolute intentions, or deeds—performed by those bodhisattvas who possess the power of aspiration through their superior vows, these cannot be easily enumerated even in as many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of eons.
At that time, Vajragarbha Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"Regarding the immeasurable and profound wisdom of the past, They did not seek to take delight in mere liberation;
Contemplating the Buddha’s wisdom and entering the Buddha’s secrets, They chose the wondrous, inconceivable knowledge."
Purifying the gates of dhāraṇī and samādhi, Attaining great supernormal powers to enter myriad lands;
Cultivating the powers, fearlessnesses, and unshared dharmas, One accords with great compassion and enters the ninth stage.
When a Bodhisattva dwells in this Stage of Excellent Intelligence, they thoroughly understand what is wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate;
they clearly know the out-flowing and the out-flow-free, the mundane and the supramundane, as well as all that is conceivable and inconceivable.
Whether phenomena are determinate or indeterminate, the practices of the three vehicles and the stage of Buddhahood;
the distinctions between conditioned and unconditioned activities—knowing them thus, one enters the world.
They are able to understand the minds of sentient beings, their afflictions, karmic retributions, and inclinations;
their spiritual lineages, dispositions, and latent tendencies, as well as the dense forest of the accumulated habitual patterns of rebirth.
Knowing that the various natures of the mind shift rapidly, possessing such characteristics as being without substance and being boundless;
that afflictions are limitless and arise from one another, dwelling together with latent tendencies and active fetters to continue the succession of rebirths.
The various natures of karma, each distinct and differentiated, And how causes perish while fruits accumulate—all this he fully knows.
The various faculties—low, middling, and superior— And their immeasurable distinctions across the past and future limits;
As well as the types of resolute understanding and inclinations, He likewise knows them all without exception.
The latent tendencies, constant delusions, and views of a self in sentient beings—this dense forest, uncut since beginningless time—arise together with mental inclinations and coexist with the mind.
Constantly bound and never severed, they are merely false conceptualizations lacking any substantial reality; they do not exist apart from the mind and have no location.
Though one practices meditative concentration and the like, it remains difficult to dispel; only the vajra path can utterly extinguish it.
The births within the six realms of existence each differ: karma is the field, craving is the moisture, and ignorance is the covering.
Consciousness is the seed and name-and-form is the sprout; thus the three realms continue in succession from beginningless time.
The accumulation of karmic tendencies, activities, afflictions, and habitual propensities gives rise again and again in succession, never free from delusion.
All sentient beings abide within the three categories: some are submerged in views, while others practice the path.
The Bodhisattvas on this stage observe them skillfully, according to their inclinations, faculties, and understandings.
With unimpeded and wondrous eloquence, he preaches the Dharma according to the specific needs of each being.
Seated upon the Dharma throne like a lion, he is also like a bull-king, a king of jewel mountains, or a dragon king spreading dense clouds;
he pours down a great rain of sweet nectar that fills the vast ocean.
Well-knowing the characteristics and profound meanings of phenomena, they are able to explain them with skillful words.
They possess a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* dhāraṇīs, like the great ocean receiving all rain;
their dhāraṇīs and samādhis are all pure, and they are able to see many Buddhas in a single thought-moment.
At each and every Buddha’s abode they hear the Dharma, And further expound it with wondrous voices;
Throughout the three thousand great thousandfold worlds as desired, They teach and transform all living beings.
Like clouds spreading vast and wide, reaching everywhere, they bring joy to all according to their faculties and inclinations;
sentient beings from the infinite worlds of the ten directions all come to draw near and sit within the assembly.
In a single thought-moment, each follows their own mind to pose difficult questions, yet with a single voice, you respond universally so that all are fully satisfied;
the assemblies of Buddhas upon the tip of a hair are beyond counting, and the inclinations of sentient beings are likewise inexhaustible.
He accords with their minds and bestows Dharma-gates; all realms of phenomena are likewise so.
Through the power of diligent and vigorous effort, the Bodhisattva further attains merit that becomes ever more supreme.
Hearing and upholding all dharma-gates as they are inscribed in words, like the earth which can sustain all seeds;
abiding here in the rank of a Crown Prince who succeeds to the Dharma, he instructs and guides according to their capacities without weariness.
Day and night he beholds the Buddha, never turning away; He enters the profound liberation of the wisdom of cessation.
His offerings to all Buddhas increase his virtue and clarity, Like a wondrous golden ornament upon a king’s crown;
Furthermore, he causes sentient beings to extinguish their afflictions, Just as the light of the Brahma King shines everywhere.
Abiding here, one often becomes a Great Brahmā King, converting sentient beings through the Dharma of the Three Vehicles;
with the wholesome karma thus performed, all are universally benefited, until finally one attains omniscience.
In a single thought-moment, one can enter into hundreds of thousands of millions of samādhis as numerous as the atoms in incalculable lands;
the same applies to seeing Buddhas and other such matters, yet what is accomplished through the power of vows exceeds even this.
This is the ninth stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence, The sphere of practice for Bodhisattvas of great wisdom;
Profound, subtle, and difficult to perceive, I have now briefly explained it for the sake of the Buddha’s sons.
The Ninth Stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (*Sādhumatī*), of the Bodhisattva is completed. The *Buddhabhāṣita-daśabhūmika-sūtra*, Scroll Seven.
The *Buddhabhāṣita-daśabhūmika-sūtra*, Scroll Eight.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīladharma, a śramaṇa from Khotan during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Translated at Longxing Monastery in Beiting. Ten:

The Bodhisattva Bhūmi of the Dharma-Cloud (Bodhisattvabhūmi-dharmameghā), Part One of Ten. Myriads of deities from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, Hearing of the supreme practices within this stage, Leaped for joy in the air with hearts full of delight, And all together made offerings to the Buddha with profound devotion.
The inconceivable assembly of bodhisattvas, likewise rejoicing greatly in the air,
all burned supreme and pleasing incense, which universally perfumed the great assembly and rendered it pure.
The Sovereign King of Heaven and his celestial hosts, numbering immeasurable billions, were in the void;
they scattered heavenly robes everywhere as offerings to the Buddha, falling in a profusion of hundreds of thousands of varieties.
The celestial maidens were beyond measure, and there was none who did not joyfully make offerings to the Buddha;
each played various kinds of exquisite music, all praising him with these words:
"The Tathāgata sits peacefully in a single land, yet manifests his body throughout all worlds."
His physical marks are majestic and infinite in number, Pervading and filling the vastness of the dharma-realm.
From a single pore he emits radiant light, Universally extinguishing the darkness of afflictions in the world;
The atoms of all lands may be counted, But the number of these rays of light cannot be known.
Sometimes they manifest as Tathāgatas endowed with all marks, turning the unsurpassed wheel of the true Dharma;
sometimes they manifest traveling through various Buddha-fields, or remaining in silent, unmoving tranquility;
sometimes they manifest dwelling in palaces of contentment, or manifest descending to enter a mother’s womb.
Sometimes they manifest dwelling in the womb or emerging from it, causing them to be seen in all immeasurable lands;
sometimes they manifest leaving home to cultivate the noble path, or manifest attaining perfect enlightenment at the site of awakening;
sometimes they manifest preaching the Dharma or entering nirvana, universally enabling those throughout the ten directions to behold them all.
Just as a magician, knowing the arts of illusion, performs many deeds amidst a great multitude;
so too is the wisdom of the Tathāgata, manifesting its body everywhere throughout the world.
The Buddha abides in the profound and true nature of phenomena, Quiescent, without marks, and identical to space;
Yet within the ultimate reality, He manifests all manner of deeds.
The activities for benefiting sentient beings in which one abides are all attained by relying on the nature of phenomena (dharmatā);
appearance and non-appearance are without distinction, for upon entering the ultimate, all are signless.
If one wishes to realize the wisdom of the Tathāgata, One should abandon all false conceptualizations;
Thoroughly penetrating both existence and non-existence as equal, One will swiftly become a great guide for humans and devas.

After the immeasurable and boundless hosts of goddesses had offered praise with various voices, their bodies and minds became tranquil and they dwelt in shared peace; gazing up at the Tathāgata, they remained silent.
At that moment, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, perceiving that the entire assembly was serene and silent,
addressed Vajragarbha with these words:
"O Great Fearless One, true Son of the Buddha!"
From the ninth stage entering the tenth, May you now proclaim for the sake of the wise All the characteristics of merit and practice,
As well as the matters of supernormal powers and transformations.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha addressed the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!

If a bodhisattva, by means of the wisdom capable of investigating such immeasurable objects of knowledge, continues until the end of the ninth bodhisattva stage, having skillfully selected and discerned, skillfully prepared the pure dharmas (*śukladharma*), skillfully accumulated the collection of boundless provisions, well-received vast merit and wisdom, realized immeasurable great loving-kindness and great compassion, understood the distinctions and classifications of worlds, entered the dense forest of the realm of sentient beings, and through mental application and conceptualization entered the sphere of the Buddhas—taking as its object the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique buddha-qualities (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*)—this is called 'having reached the stage of being consecrated for all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), which is the culmination of all aspects.'"
O Son of the Buddha!

When this bodhisattva has already been able to accord with such wisdom-conduct and has entered the stage of the Bodhisattva’s consecration (*abhiṣeka*), there appear before him the great samādhi called "Stainless," the samādhi called "Discerning the Differentiations of the Dharmadhātu," the samādhi called "Adorning the Bodhimaṇḍa," the samādhi called "Flower-Glory of All Modes," the samādhi called "Ocean-Treasury Adornment," the samādhi called "Ocean-Seal," the samādhi called "Vastness of the Space-Element," the samādhi called "Selecting the Self-Nature of All Phenomena," the samādhi called "Accordance with the Mental Conduct of All Sentient Beings," and the samādhi called "All Buddhas of the Present Dwelling Before One. These samādhis manifest before him.

Thus, these one million *asaṃkhyeya* samādhis, headed by this foremost one, all manifest before the bodhisattva; the bodhisattva enters and emerges from these samādhis with mastery, and having attained skill in these samādhis, he even manifests the performance of all activities associated with meditative concentration (*samādhi*).
Then, for this bodhisattva, up to one million asaṃkhyeya samādhis later, the great samādhi of consecration called "The Excellence of Omniscient Wisdom" manifests before him.

As soon as this samādhi manifests, a great jewel-king lotus appears; its magnitude equals a million triple-thousand great thousandfold world systems. It is adorned with an intermingling of various exquisite jewels, transcending all worldly realms. Born from supramundane roots of virtue, it has an illusory nature and is formed by objective conditions. Established upon the dharmadhātu and appearing as its reflection, it is not something that can exist within the abodes of the gods.

Its stem was made of mahāvaiḍūrya maṇi jewels; its pedestal was made of incomparable king-sandalwood; its filaments were of agate; its petals were of Jambūnada gold. It possessed immeasurable radiance, shimmering with various famous flowers, and its interior was inlaid with all manner of exquisite gems. It was covered by a boundless net of jewels and was accompanied by a retinue of lotuses as numerous as the atoms within a million triple-thousand great thousandfold world systems.

At that time, the Bodhisattva’s physical form was exquisitely beautiful and perfectly proportioned to his lotus; because the Great Samādhi of the Consecration of the Supreme Wisdom of Omniscience had manifested before him, he displayed himself sitting upon a throne of a precious king-lotus.

As soon as the Bodhisattva had sat upon this seat, as many Bodhisattva followers as there were lotus attendants on that wondrous Great Jewel King Lotus Throne also came and sat upon them, surrounding this great Bodhisattva on all sides. They gazed up at the body of the great Bodhisattva with reverence, and each individual Bodhisattva attained one million samādhis.

When this Great Bodhisattva and his retinue, along with all the bodhisattvas, enter meditative absorption, all worlds tremble greatly; all evil realms are completely stilled; light shines universally throughout the entire dharma-realm; all worlds become thoroughly adorned and purified; all sounds and voices within all Buddha-fields are heard; all bodhisattvas who practice in common assemble there without exception; the music of humans and devas in all worlds sounds forth simultaneously; all sentient beings attain peace and happiness; and inconceivable offerings and services are performed simultaneously before all Buddhas, the Truly and Fully Enlightened Ones, as witnessed by the assemblies of all Buddhas in the ten directions.
Why is this so? O Son of the Buddha!

As soon as the Bodhisattva has sat upon this great jewel-king lotus throne, he emits from his two feet a million *asaṃkhyeya* rays of light that universally illuminate the ten directions, reaching down as far as the Avīci Great Hell to eliminate and extinguish all suffering there.
From his two kneecaps, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which universally illuminated all realms of animals throughout the ten directions, extinguishing their suffering.
From the circle of his navel, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which universally illuminated all realms of Yama throughout the ten directions, extinguishing their suffering.
From his left and right sides, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which universally illumined the bodies of all people throughout the ten directions, extinguishing their suffering.
From the palms of both hands, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which universally illumined the palaces where all the devas and asuras dwell throughout the ten directions.
From his two shoulders, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which universally illuminated the assemblies of śrāvakas throughout the ten directions.
From his neck and back, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which universally illuminated the bodies of the pratyekabuddhas throughout the ten directions.
From his face, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which universally illuminated all bodhisattvas from their first resolve up to the ninth stage throughout the ten directions.

From the mark of the white tuft between his brows, he emitted millions of asaṃkhyeya rays of light, which eclipsed all the palaces of the māras throughout the worlds of the ten directions and illuminated the great bodhisattvas who had attained the stage of empowerment; having shone upon them, the light remained.

From the crown of his head, he emitted millions of *asaṃkhyeya* times the number of dust motes in a trichiliocosm of worlds as rays of light, which universally illuminated the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas throughout the ten directions. After circling to the right ten kinds of worldly realms, they remained suspended in the void, forming a vast wheel of light-nets that performed a great offering before all the Buddhas, known as "Blazing Radiance."

From the first generation of the mind of enlightenment up to the ninth stage, the immeasurable offerings made to the Buddhas throughout those transitions do not equal even one hundredth of this; they do not equal one thousandth, one hundred-thousandth, one koṭi-th, one hundred-koṭi-th, one thousand-koṭi-th, one hundred-thousand-koṭi-th, or even one hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta-th part; they cannot be reached by calculation, analogy, or even by the fraction known as the *upaniṣad*.

From that vast wheel of the net of light, there rained down various exquisite incenses—burnt, unguent, and powdered—as well as flower garlands, robes, banners, pennants, precious parasols, jeweled necklaces, *maṇi* gems, and other ornaments of adornment. Like great clouds pouring down heavy rain, all these things surpassed everything else in all the worlds; they were produced by the power of supramundane, superior roots of goodness and reached before the assemblies of each and every Tathāgata throughout the ten directions, serving as offerings to all the Buddhas.
If any sentient beings were to perceive such a great offering as this, they would all attain non-retrogression from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Having performed these acts of worship through the transformation of these rays of light, and having illuminated the assemblies of all Tathāgatas and circumambulated the ten kinds of worlds to the right, they entered through the soles of the feet of all the Tathāgatas.

At that time, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas immediately came to know that in a certain world, a certain great Bodhisattva had accomplished such vast and correct practice as to reach the stage of consecration.
“O Son of the Buddha!

At that time, the bodhisattva assemblies from the ten directions—immeasurable, boundless, and including those up to the ninth stage—all come to surround him and present great offerings. When all gaze upon this bodhisattva, each attains one million samādhis.”

At that time, all the great Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions who had already received empowerment each emitted from the mark of virtue upon their vajra-ornamented chests a great light named "Able to Subjugate All Māras and Enemies," with a retinue of hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* lights, universally illuminating the ten directions and manifesting immeasurable supernatural transformations.
Having performed these deeds, they enter into this mark of the Bodhisattva’s virtue, the adamantine adornment upon the chest;
once their light has entered, it causes the Bodhisattva’s wisdom and majestic power to increase, surpassing what was before by more than a hundred thousandfold.
“O Son of the Buddha!

At that time, all the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the ten directions, each emitted from the mark of the white tuft between their eyebrows a great radiance called ‘Possessing the Supernatural Power of the Nature of All-Knowledge,’ with countless rays of light as its retinue.”
That light universally illumined all worlds throughout the ten directions without exception, circumambulated the ten kinds of all worlds to the right,
and manifested the vast and magnificent displays of the Tathāgata. It awakened immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas,
caused all buddha-fields to quake in six ways, and brought all [afflictions] to rest.
It eclipses all the perilous evil realms and the cycle of birth and death;
it universally reveals the seats of perfect enlightenment where all Tathāgatas attain the Way;
it manifests the assemblies of all Buddhas, their majestic adornments shining forth everywhere throughout all worlds as far as the reaches of the Dharma-realm and the nature of empty space.
Then, the great radiance returned to this assembly of all bodhisattvas, surrounding them on all sides;
having completed the manifestation of vast and magnificent adornments, it entered through the crowns of the great bodhisattvas,
and the attendant rays of light likewise each entered the crowns of the bodhisattvas seated in that gathered assembly.

When the light enters, those bodhisattvas each attain one million samādhis that they had not previously attained. Once these lights have simultaneously entered the crown of this bodhisattva’s head, he is said to have received the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) within the sphere of the Buddha; if he fulfills the ten powers, he is then reckoned among the ranks of the Perfectly Awakened Ones (*samyaksaṃbuddha*).
"O Son of the Buddha!
It is like the crown prince of a wheel-turning sage king, born of the principal queen and endowed with the marks of royalty.

That wheel-turning king causes this prince to sit upon a magnificent golden throne atop a white elephant treasure; he spreads a great net-like canopy, erects great banners and pennants, and provides flower parasols, garments, burning incense, scattered flowers, powdered incense, floral garlands, and the playing of various musical instruments. He then commands that the waters of the four great oceans from the four continents be taken and placed within a golden pitcher."

The Wheel-Turning Sage King personally holds the vessel and pours water over the crown of the prince’s head; as soon as the consecration is completed, he is reckoned among the number of consecrated Kṣatriya kings. However, it is only when he fully practices the ten paths of wholesome action that he is truly entitled to be called a Wheel-Turning Sage King.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is the same for the bodhisattva: as soon as they have received the empowerment from all Buddhas, they are said to have received the empowerment of the water of wisdom; once they are perfected in the ten powers, they enter the rank of the Truly and Fully Enlightened Ones.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva’s Mahāyāna consecration.
For the sake of this consecration, the Bodhisattva initiates immeasurable hundreds of thousands of difficult practices.
Having thus received the empowerment, the Bodhisattva increases immeasurable wisdom and merit, and is said to be "dwelling securely within the Dharma-Cloud Stage.
"O Son of the Buddha!

When a bodhisattva dwells in this stage of the Cloud of Dharma, they know the origin of the desire realm, the origin of the form realm, the origin of the formless realm, the origin of the realm of sentient beings, the origin of the realm of consciousness, the origin of the conditioned realm, the origin of the unconditioned realm, the origin of the realm of space, the origin of the realm of phenomena, and the origin of the realm of nirvāṇa; all these they know as they truly are.

He thoroughly understands and perceives the accumulation of afflictions through conduct; the accumulation of the formation and destruction of worlds; the accumulation of the conduct of śrāvakas; the accumulation of the conduct of pratyekabuddhas; the accumulation of the conduct of bodhisattvas; the accumulation of the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique buddha-qualities of a Buddha, as well as the form-body and dharma-body; the accumulation of the omniscient wisdom in all its aspects; the accumulation of manifesting perfect enlightenment, turning the great wheel of Dharma, and entering parinirvāṇa; and the accumulation of entering into the analytical and clear elucidation of all phenomena.
To state the essentials: by means of the accumulation of all-aspect omniscience (*sarvākāra-sarvajñajñāna*), they know everything as it truly is.

Furthermore, by relying on such wisdom that accords with knowledge (*anujñāna-anugata-prajñā*), these bodhisattvas gradually come to understand the transformations of sentient beings, the transformations of karma and afflictions, the transformations of views and conduct, the transformations of world-systems, the transformations of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), the transformations of śrāvakas, the transformations of pratyekabuddhas, the transformations of bodhisattvas, and the transformations of tathāgatas; they know the non-conceptual nature of all these various transformations as they truly are.

Furthermore, this bodhisattva knows the empowerment of the Buddha, the empowerment of the Dharma, the empowerment of the Saṅgha, the empowerment of karma, the empowerment of afflictions, the empowerment of time, the empowerment of vows, the empowerment of offerings, the empowerment of right practice, the empowerment of eons, and the empowerment of wisdom; all these he knows as they truly are.
Furthermore, this bodhisattva thoroughly understands the subtle wisdom with which the Buddhas, the Truly Perfectly Awakened Ones, enter [into various states], namely:

either entering the subtle wisdom of conduct; or entering the subtle wisdom of descending to take birth; or entering the subtle wisdom of birth; or entering the subtle wisdom of playful manifestation; or entering the subtle wisdom of renouncing the world; or entering the subtle wisdom of attaining perfect awakening; or entering the subtle wisdom of turning the wheel of Dharma; or entering the subtle wisdom of empowerment and deliberation; or entering the subtle wisdom of parinirvāṇa; or entering the subtle wisdom of the endurance of the Dharma—all of these he knows exactly as they are.
Furthermore, this bodhisattva thoroughly understands all the secret aspects of the Buddha, the Truly Perfectly Awakened One, namely:

the secrets of body; the secrets of speech; the secrets of mind; the secrets of deliberating upon the appropriate and inappropriate times; the secrets of bestowing predictions of enlightenment upon bodhisattvas; the secrets of gathering and subduing sentient beings; the secrets of the various distinctions among vehicles; the secrets of the distinctions in the faculties and conduct of sentient beings; the secrets of entering into the functioning of all karmic actions; and the secrets of the nature of practicing, attaining the path, and awakening—all of these he knows as they truly are.
Furthermore, this bodhisattva thoroughly understands all the wisdom regarding the entry into eons possessed by all Buddhas; that is to say:
sometimes one eon enters into countless eons, or countless eons enter into one eon;
sometimes a finite number of eons enter into countless eons, or countless eons enter into a finite number of eons; or a single kṣaṇa enters into...
Eons enter into a single kṣaṇa; eons may enter non-eons, and non-eons may enter eons.
There may be the entry of an eon with a Buddha into an eon without a Buddha, or an eon without a Buddha into an eon with a Buddha.
There may be entry into a buddha-less realm, or entry into a realm with a Buddha. Or an eon of the past may enter the future or the present, or the present...
Eons of the past enter the future, and eons of the future enter the past and present;
long eons enter short eons, and short eons enter long eons; short eons enter non-short eons, and non-short eons enter short eons.
Within all such eons, the activities of entering and the characteristics of entry—all of these are exactly as they truly are.
He knows. Furthermore, this bodhisattva thoroughly understands all the wisdoms of entry possessed by the Buddhas, the Truly Perfectly Awakened Ones, namely:

the wisdom of entering the path of ignorance; the wisdom of entering the knowledge of atoms; the wisdom of entering the perfect awakening to lands and bodies; the wisdom of entering the perfect awakening to the bodies and minds of sentient beings; the wisdom of entering the perfect awakening that accords with all places; the wisdom of entering the manifestation of erratic conduct; the wisdom of entering the manifestation of conforming conduct; the wisdom of entering the manifestation of contrary conduct; the wisdom of entering the manifestation of conceivable and inconceivable, or discernible and indiscernible worldly conduct; and the wisdom of entering the manifestation of what is known by śrāvakas, what is known by pratyekabuddhas, what is known by bodhisattvas, and what is known by Tathāgatas—all of these he knows as they truly are.
"O Son of the Buddha, the wisdom of all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, is vast and immeasurable; within this stage, the wisdom entered by the Bodhisattva is likewise immeasurable.
"O Son of the Buddha!

Furthermore, as the Bodhisattva thus accords with the practice of this stage, they attain the Bodhisattva’s inconceivable liberation, the unobstructed liberation, the liberation of pure discernment, the liberation of universal manifestation, the liberation of the Tathāgatagarbha, the liberation that accords with the wheel of non-obstruction, the liberation that accords with the activities of the three periods of time, the liberation of the treasury of the Dharma-realm, the liberation of the radiant light of the wheel of liberation, and the liberation of the realm without remainder."
O Son of the Buddha!

When a bodhisattva dwells in this tenth stage, the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā bhūmi*), these ten liberations serve as the foremost; they attain immeasurable and incalculable hundreds of thousands of gates of liberation. Likewise, they attain immeasurable and incalculable hundreds of thousands of samādhis, immeasurable and incalculable hundreds of thousands of dhāraṇīs, and they attain the manifestation of immeasurable and incalculable hundreds of thousands of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
“O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva, having accomplished such wisdom that accords with knowledge and the power of mindfulness that accords with immeasurable skillful means, is able—in a single kṣaṇa, an instant, a mere moment—to endure, receive, grasp, and universally sustain all the immeasurable great Dharma-lights, the immeasurable great Dharma-illuminations, and the immeasurable clouds of the Great Dharma belonging to the infinite Tathāgatas of the ten directions.”
O Son of the Buddha!
It is, for example, like the clouds of the Sāgara Dragon pouring down a great mass of water; except for the great ocean, no other place is able to receive, sustain, or support it.
All that the Buddhas enter into the secret treasury of the Buddha— namely, the great light of the Dharma,

the great illumination of the Dharma, and the great cloud of the Dharma— is likewise something that these sentient beings, the assembly of śrāvakas, all pratyekabuddhas, and all bodhisattvas from the first to the ninth bhūmi cannot endure, cannot receive, cannot take up, and cannot sustain.
When a bodhisattva dwells in this stage of the Cloud of Dharma, they are able to endure all of these, receive them all, fully embrace them, and universally sustain them.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like the great ocean, which can endure, receive, fully embrace, and universally sustain all the great rains poured down by a single great dragon king.

Whether it be two, three, or even immeasurable great dragon kings, the heavy rains they pour down in a single kṣaṇa, muhūrta, or instant, he is able to endure them all, receive them all, take them all in, and universally sustain them all.
Why is this? Because the great ocean is immeasurable in its length and breadth.
O Son of the Buddha!

When a bodhisattva dwells in this stage of the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā), it is likewise so: before a single Buddha, they are able, in a single kṣaṇa, muhūrta, or moment, to endure, receive, grasp, and sustain immeasurable clarities of the Dharma, illuminations of the Dharma, and clouds of the Dharma.

Before two, three, or even immeasurable Tathāgatas, one is able, in a single kṣaṇa, muhūrta, or moment, to endure, receive, grasp, and sustain immeasurable radiance of Dharma, illumination of Dharma, and clouds of Dharma; for this reason, this stage is called the Cloud of Dharma (Dharmameghā).
The Bodhisattva Vimukticandra said: "O Son of the Buddha!

How could one possibly calculate the number of Buddhas that these bodhisattvas of this stage can, in a single kṣaṇa, muhūrta, or moment, endure, receive, embrace, and sustain the great light of the Dharma, the great illumination of the Dharma, and the great clouds of the Dharma?"
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva said:
"O Son of the Buddha!
This matter cannot be explained by means of calculation."

Bodhisattvas on this stage are able, in a single kṣaṇa, muhūrta, or moment, before various Tathāgatas, to receive, experience, grasp, and sustain the great light of the Dharma, the great illumination of the Dharma, and the clouds of the Dharma; however, for your sake, O Noble One, I shall provide an analogy.
O Son of the Buddha!

Suppose, for example, that within all the realms of sentient beings—without exception—in as many worlds as there are atoms in ten million *koṭi-nayuta* unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, there were a certain sentient being who had attained the supreme *dhāraṇī* of hearing and retention (*śrutadhara-dhāraṇī*) and served as an attendant to a Buddha, becoming the foremost among the assembly of *śrāvakas* in great learning, just like the Greatly Victorious Bhikṣu under the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vajrapadmagarbha.

Suppose one sentient being were to achieve such power of mastery through extensive learning (*bahuśruta*), and suppose every other sentient being in all world-systems without exception were likewise to achieve such power of dhāraṇī through extensive learning; yet, whatever dharma one sentient being has received, no other would receive again.
"O Son of the Buddha! What do you think?
Is the erudition and skill of those sentient beings not truly immeasurable?"
The Bodhisattva Vimukticandra said:
"O Son of the Buddha!
Those sentient beings possess vast and immeasurable erudition and skill."
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva said:
"O Son of the Buddha!
I shall now inform you so that you may attain understanding."

When a bodhisattva dwells securely in the stage of the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā), in a single moment before a single Buddha, that which is entrusted, received, gathered, and sustained by them is called the Great Dharma-Light, the Dharma-Illumination, and the Dharma-Cloud of the Treasury of the Dharma-Dhātu of the Three Times.

Compared to this skillful mastery of sustaining the cloud-illumination of the light of this Great Dharma, the skill in erudition possessed by all those sentient beings in the aforementioned worlds does not approach even a hundredth part; it does not approach a thousandth, a hundred-thousandth, a koṭi-th, a hundred-koṭi-th, a thousand-koṭi-th, a hundred-thousand-koṭi-th, or a hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta-th part;
it cannot be reached even by calculation, analogy, or even by the upaniṣad-th part.

Just as it is at the site of one Buddha, so too at the sites of as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones as there are atoms in all the worlds throughout the ten directions as previously described, and even beyond that number—at the sites of immeasurable and boundless Tathāgatas—they are able, in a single kṣaṇa, a moment, or an instant, to endure, receive, grasp, and sustain all the great dharma-lights, dharma-illuminations, and dharma-clouds of the Dharma-realm treasury belonging to the three times; therefore, this stage is named "Dharma Cloud" (Dharmameghā).
"Furthermore, Sons of the Buddha!

Once a Bodhisattva has become firmly established in the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā bhūmi*), from this power of aspiration they raise clouds of great compassion and thunder the great Dharma-thunder. The lightning-flash of supernatural powers and fearlessness blazes forth; the wind of great radiance whirls rapidly and spreads afar; and a thick mist of great merit and wisdom completely covers all. They manifest various bodies that gather and disperse like dark clouds;

they let out the great lion’s roar to terrify and crush the armies of Māra, pervading the ten directions in a single *kṣaṇa*, a moment, or an instant—throughout the worlds previously described, numbering as many as the atoms within them, and even exceeding that number."

It universally covers immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of worlds, pouring down the great, incomparable rain of the nectar-like Dharma; it extinguishes the flames of the dust of various delusions arising from the ignorance of sentient beings, and causes the crops of their roots of goodness to grow and ripen according to their inclinations. For this reason, this stage is named "Dharma Cloud" (Dharmameghā).
"Furthermore, Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva dwells in this Dharma-Cloud Stage (Dharmameghā-bhūmi), within a single world-system—beginning from his residence in the Tuṣita Heaven—he manifests all manner of Buddha-activities according to the inclinations of sentient beings who are to be liberated: descending, entering the womb, dwelling and being born, renouncing the world, attaining enlightenment, accepting invitations to turn the Great Wheel of Dharma, and returning to Great Nirvāṇa. This extends to two, three, or even as many worlds as there are atoms in the aforementioned worlds, and further beyond that number, into immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of worlds; beginning from his residence in the Tuṣita Heaven therein, up to manifesting entry into Great Parinirvāṇa, he displays all manner of Buddha-activities according to the inclinations of sentient beings who are to be liberated."

When a bodhisattva has thus attained mastery over wisdom through excellent discernment, they exercise great wisdom and supernormal powers according to their own mental inclinations. They can manifest a narrow world as vast and a vast world as narrow;
furthermore, according to their will, they can manifest a defiled world as pure and a pure world as defiled.

In this way, by virtue of their sovereign power over all worlds—whether vast or immeasurable, coarse or subtle, disordered, orderly, inverted, or upright—they are able to bring forth all manner of such manifestations.

Alternatively, according to the bodhisattva’s mental aspiration, he may place a single world-system within a single atom, extending all the way to the edge of the Cakravāḍa mountains; yet the atom does not increase in size nor does the world-system decrease, while the entire operation is made fully manifest.

Furthermore, within a single atom, one may place two, three, four, five, or even unspeakably many worlds; each world is perfectly complete, extending individually to the limits of the Cakravāḍa mountains, yet the substance and appearance of that atom remain as they were, while all the worlds within it become clearly manifest.
Or, according to their mental inclinations, they may manifest within a single world the adornments of two worlds, even manifesting the adornments of unspeakably many worlds.
Or, according to their mental inclinations, they are able to display the adornments of a single world within two worlds, and even manifest them within unspeakable numbers of worlds.

Furthermore, according to their inclinations and desires, they are able to manifest themselves before all sentient beings throughout even unspeakably many worlds; yet, within a single world, they do not cause any affliction or distress to those beings.

Furthermore, according to their inclinations and desires, whatever realms of sentient beings exist within a single world-system, he manifests them throughout unspeakably many world-systems, yet without causing any affliction or distress to those sentient beings.

Furthermore, according to their wishes, they manifest the adornments of the realm of a single Buddha within a single hair-pore, even manifesting the adornments of the realms of all unspeakably many Buddhas.

Furthermore, according to his heart's desire, in a single kṣaṇa, an instant, or a brief moment, he manifests bodies as numerous as the atoms within unspeakable numbers of worlds. Within each body, he displays hands as numerous as the atoms of dust, and with these hands, he reverently makes offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions. With each hand, he holds flower caskets as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and scatters them over the Buddhas; likewise, he does the same with incense boxes, flower garlands, ointments, powdered incense, robes, precious canopies, banners, pennants, and all manner of ornaments.

Within each and every body, he further manifests as many heads as there are atoms; within each head, he empowers as many tongues as there are atoms, using all these tongues to praise the merits of the Buddhas of the ten directions.

Furthermore, within each and every moment of thought, they traverse the ten directions; in the space of a single thought-moment, they universally manifest throughout the ten directions, demonstrating the attainment of perfect enlightenment up to the entry into nirvana, sustaining the adornments of the lands, and manifesting infinite bodies throughout the three periods of time.

Or, within their own bodies, they manifest immeasurable Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and the infinite, boundless adornments of Buddha-fields; they can manifest within their own bodies the formation and destruction of all worlds, and from a single pore, they can draw forth all wind-wheels according to their wish, yet without causing any harm or affliction to sentient beings.

Furthermore, according to the inclinations of his mind, he manifests a single great ocean within infinite worlds; within the waters of this ocean, a great lotus flower appears, its radiant adornments filling immeasurable and boundless worlds. Within it, he manifests the splendors of the Great Bodhi tree, even manifesting the attainment of the nature of omniscience (sarvajñatā) through its correspondence with all supreme and wondrous qualities.

Alternatively, within their own bodies, they manifest all the radiance of the mani-jewels of the worlds of the ten directions; the light of the sun, moon, stars, constellations, clouds, lightning, and so forth, appears therein without exception.
By exhaling a breath from their mouths, they can cause immeasurable worlds in the ten directions to tremble, yet without causing sentient beings therein to feel fear or alarm.

Furthermore, they manifest the wind, fire, and water calamities of the ten directions; according to their will and desire, they are able to empower the physical bodies of all sentient beings so that they are adorned with excellence.

Sometimes they manifest the body of a Buddha within their own bodies; sometimes they manifest their own bodies within the body of a Buddha; sometimes they manifest buddha-fields within the body of a Buddha; and sometimes they manifest the body of a Buddha within a buddha-field.
O Son of the Buddha!

Having established themselves in the Dharma-Cloud Stage, Bodhisattvas are able to manifest these and other countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of supernatural transformations and playful displays.
The Scripture on the Ten Stages Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll Eight;
The Scripture on the Ten Stages Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll Nine.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīladharma of Khotan during the Great Tang Dynasty.

This is the continuation of the translation of the *Bodhisattvabhūmi* (The Stage of the Bodhisattva’s Cloud of Dharma) at Longxing Monastery in Beiting. At that time, a certain class of bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakras, Brahmās, Lokapālas, Maheśvaras, and the assembly of Śuddhāvāsa devas, each gave rise to this thought:
"If the scope of the bodhisattva’s power of knowledge regarding the characteristics of supernormal activities is thus immeasurable, what then can be said of the Buddha?"
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra, having understood the thoughts in the minds of the assembled multitude, addressed the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha in gold-colored light:
"O Son of the Buddha!
Now this great assembly, hearing of the bodhisattva’s power of supernatural penetrations and wisdom, has fallen into a web of doubt. Excellent,
O Benevolent One!
"To sever that doubt, I shall briefly manifest the matters of the Bodhisattva’s majestic adornment of spiritual transformations.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha entered the bodhisattva samādhi called "Manifesting the Essential Nature of All Buddha-fields."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha entered the bodhisattva samādhi called "Manifesting the Essential Nature of All Buddha-fields. Once he had entered it, all the hosts of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, Śakras, Brahmās, world-protectors, Maheśvaras, and Śuddhāvāsa devas saw themselves within the body of the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha;

therein they further beheld the manifestation of a Buddha-field, with all its various modes of adornment within that field, such that even if one were to speak for a full *koṭi* of great eons, one could not exhaustively describe them.

Furthermore, within that very place, he saw a Bodhi tree; its circumference was equal to a million sets of three thousand worlds, its branches and twigs were luxuriantly interlaced and immeasurably high and wide, and its spreading shade completely covered a koṭi of trichiliocosms.
Corresponding to the dimensions of the tree’s form was a lion throne, upon which he saw the Buddha named Sarvābhijñājñānarāja Tathāgata, seated beneath the tree at the site of enlightenment.
Thus, the various kinds of wondrous adornments manifested therein could not be fully described even if one were to speak for ten million great kalpas.

When the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha had displayed such a great supernatural manifestation, he caused the entire assembly of bodhisattvas, as well as all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, Brahmā, the world-protectors, Maheśvara, and the hosts of Śuddhāvāsika devas, each to return to their respective places.
At that time, the great assembly gave rise to thoughts of unprecedented wonder; they remained silent, gazing single-mindedly toward the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra addressed the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!
How truly marvelous and rare this is!"
This samādhi is fully endowed with such majestic power and adornment.
Son of the Buddha!
What is the name of this samādhi?
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva said:
"This samādhi is named 'Manifesting the Essential Nature of All Buddha-fields.
Vimukticandra Bodhisattva asked:
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the array of the objective realm traversed by this samādhi?
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva replied:
“O Son of the Buddha!

Because the Bodhisattva cultivates this samādhi, he is able to manifest within his own body as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in the worlds of the Ganges River as previously seen; furthermore, he manifests even more than that number of immeasurable fields within his body, as previously seen.”
O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva dwells in this Dharma-Cloud Stage (Dharmameghā-bhūmi), they attain hundreds of thousands of such immeasurable samādhis. For this reason, other Bodhisattvas—even those who have attained the rank of a Dharma Prince and dwell in the Bodhisattva Stage of Good Intelligence (Sādhumatī)—are unable to fathom the body or bodily actions, speech or verbal actions, or mind or mental actions of a Bodhisattva on this stage; nor can they fathom their sovereign mastery of supernatural powers in observing the three periods of time, the range of activity of their various samādhis as they enter the realm of wisdom, or their playful engagement with all gates of liberation.

One cannot fathom or know their various transformative activities, or their sustaining activities, or their activities of majestic power; to speak briefly, even the assembly of bodhisattvas who have already attained the rank of Dharma Prince and abide in the Bodhisattva stage of Good Intelligence cannot fathom the activities of this [eighth] stage bodhisattva, even down to the mere lifting and lowering of his feet.
O Son of the Buddha!

This Bodhisattva’s Stage of the Cloud of Dharma is thus immeasurable; it is described here only in brief, for were it to be explained in detail, even if one were to expound it for hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, one could not exhaust it.
The Bodhisattva Vimukticandra said:
"O Son of the Buddha!
If the empowerment of the bodhisattvas' sphere of correct practice within this is thus immeasurable, what then is the entry into the sphere of the Tathāgata's own practice?"
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva said:
"O Son of the Buddha!
It is as if a person were to take one, two, or three pebbles, each as large as a jujube pit, from the four-continent world-system and say: "
"Is the amount of earth in the elemental earth of infinite world-systems greater, or is this [other] greater?

My observation of your question is likewise so: how can you now compare the incomparable dharma-nature of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and the one of immeasurable wisdom, with the dharma-nature of the various bodhisattvas?
However, son of good family!
Just as the sand and pebbles taken from a portion of the earth in the world of four continents are extremely few, while the remainder is truly immeasurable;
so it is, O Son of the Buddha!

In this same way, even if one were to expound upon this Bodhisattva stage of the Cloud of Dharma for immeasurable eons, one could only explain a single portion of its meaning; how much more so, then, regarding the stage of the Tathāgata!
O Son of the Buddha!
I now tell you so that you may understand: the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, is seated before me and acts as my witness.
O Son of the Buddha!

Suppose that in each of the ten directions there were as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in boundless worlds, and that each of these fields were filled with Bodhisattvas who have attained this stage—dense as a grove of sugarcane, bamboo, rice, hemp, or forest thickets. Even the wisdom derived from the correct practice of the Bodhisattva path by all those Bodhisattvas throughout immeasurable eons cannot equal even one hundredth part of the Tathāgata’s domain; it does not equal one thousandth, one hundred-thousandth, one koṭith part, one hundred-koṭith part, one thousand-koṭith part, one hundred-thousand-koṭith part, or one hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta part. It cannot be reached even by calculation, analogy, or even by the *upaniṣad* (infinitesimal) fraction.
O Son of the Buddha!

A bodhisattva who accords with such wisdom-conduct does not differ from the bodily, verbal, and mental actions of the Tathāgata; without relinquishing the power of the bodhisattva’s samādhi, they behold all Buddhas and serve and make offerings to them.

In each and every eon, they worship immeasurable Buddhas with all kinds of supreme and wondrous offerings as appropriate; yet they are able to fully receive the empowerment and manifestation of all those Buddhas and Tathāgatas, becoming ever more exalted. Within the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), they skillfully explain all challenges and questions. For immeasurable hundreds of eons, immeasurable thousands of eons, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of eons, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of *nayuta* eons, immeasurable *koṭi* eons, immeasurable hundreds of *koṭi* eons, immeasurable thousands of *koṭi* eons, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of *koṭi* eons, and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of *koṭi-nayuta* eons, none are able to defeat them.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like a skilled goldsmith who fashions a magnificent ornament from pure, natural gold, inlaid with great maṇi jewels. When the Sovereign King of the Gods wears it upon his head or fastens it around his neck, no other ornaments or decorations of the gods can compare to it.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is likewise for a bodhisattva dwelling in this Dharma-Cloud Stage (*dharmameghā bhūmi*): this course of wisdom cannot be eclipsed; it cannot be matched by the wisdom-courses of any sentient beings, any śrāvakas, any pratyekabuddhas, or any bodhisattvas from the first stage up to the ninth stage.

The light of wisdom of the bodhisattvas on this stage can cause sentient beings to enter even into the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), and it cannot be eclipsed by any other light of knowledge.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as the light of the Great Lord Maheśvara transcends all places of birth and is able to bring joy and serenity to the bodies and minds of sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!

For a bodhisattva who dwells in this tenth stage, the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā*), the light of their wisdom is likewise such that it cannot be reached by the light of wisdom of any śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, nor by any bodhisattva dwelling from the first stage up to the ninth stage; it enables sentient beings to abide within the *dharmatā* of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).
O Son of the Buddha! When a bodhisattva has thus been able to act in accordance with wisdom,

the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, further expound for them the knowledge that penetrates the three periods of time, the knowledge of the distinctions within the dharma-realm, the knowledge that pervades all worlds, the knowledge that illumines the sustaining power throughout all worlds, and the knowledge of the lands and dharmas of all classes of sentient beings.

To state the essentials: even when teaching up to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), among the ten perfections (pāramitā), the perfection of wisdom is preeminent; yet he does not fail to practice the remaining perfections, according to his strength and capacity.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is called a brief explanation of the Bodhisattva’s tenth stage, the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā*).
Were it to be explained in detail, even if one were to spend immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, one could not reach its end.”

When Bodhisattvas dwell in this stage, they are mostly reborn as the Great Lord (Maheśvara) King of Gods; possessing mastery over the Dharma, they are able to bestow upon sentient beings the practices for reaching the other shore (pāramitā) as Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and all Bodhisattvas. Within the questions and answers concerning the distinctions of the Dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), there is no one capable of defeating them.

Whatever deeds they perform—whether through giving, kind speech, beneficial conduct, or cooperation—all of these are never apart from the mental engagement with the Buddha, the mental engagement with the Dharma, the mental engagement with the Saṅgha, the mental engagement with bodhisattvas, the mental engagement with the bodhisattva practices, the mental engagement with the perfections, the mental engagement with the stages, the mental engagement with the powers of a buddha, the mental engagement with the fearlessnesses, the mental engagement with the unique qualities of a buddha, and even up to the mental engagement with the omniscient wisdom that is perfectly conjoined with all supreme and sublime aspects.
One should constantly make this vow, saying:

"Among all sentient beings, I shall be the foremost, the most excellent, the most distinguished, the sublime, the most exquisite, the superior, the unsurpassed, the guide, the leader, and the commander; even unto attaining the state that serves as the basis for the knowledge of all-knowledge."
If one delights in initiating such diligence, by means of this diligence, in a single kṣaṇa, muhūrta, or tat-kṣaṇa,
one attains as many samādhis as there are atoms in ten million *koṭi-nayuta* unspeakable Buddha-fields,
and is able to see as many [Buddhas] as there are atoms in ten million *koṭi-nayuta* unspeakable Buddha-fields.
They can understand the empowerments (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of dust;
they can shake worlds as numerous as the atoms of dust in millions of billions of trillions of unspeakable Buddha-fields;
they can travel to Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms of dust in millions of billions of trillions of unspeakable Buddha-fields; and they can illuminate millions...
In worlds as numerous as the atoms within koṭī-nayuta buddha-fields,
they bring to maturity sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within a hundred thousand koṭī-nayuta unspeakable buddha-fields;
they abide for a lifespan of a hundred thousand koṭī-nayuta unspeakable buddha-field atoms of kalpas, entering into the past and future limits each for a hundred [kalpas].
For as many eons as there are atoms in ten million *koṭi-nayuta* unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields,
he contemplates and discerns as many Dharma-gates as there are atoms in ten million *koṭi-nayuta* unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
he manifests as many bodies as there are atoms in ten million *koṭi-nayuta* unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, and each and every body is capable of manifesting...
He was surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of unspeakable buddha-fields.

From this point upward, regarding the playful manifestations of those bodhisattvas who possess the power of vows— whether through their superior vows, or their bodies, or their radiance, or their supernormal powers, or their eyes, or their spheres of experience, or their voices, or their conduct, or their adornments, or their resolute understandings, or their deeds— it would not be easy to enumerate them even in as many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These ten stages of wisdom of the bodhisattvas are all in accord with one another, because the knowledge of all-knowledge in all its aspects gradually manifests before them.
O Son of the Buddha!

For example, just as the water flowing from Lake Anavatapta pours forth through the mouths of the four rivers to moisten and nourish the land of Jambudvīpa—neither exhausting nor diminishing, yet ever increasing until it enters the ocean and fills it to the brim.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is likewise with the roots of goodness that flow forth from the bodhicitta: through the great vows they stream forth the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), filling and benefiting the realm of all sentient beings without end, further increasing until they enter the ocean of omniscience and fill it completely.
“O Son of the Buddha!
These ten stages of the bodhisattvas are manifested based upon the Buddha-wisdom.
O Son of the Buddha!”
For example, it is like the ten great mountain kings that become manifest by depending upon the earth as their cause. What are these ten?
They are as follows:

The King of Snow Mountains, the King of Fragrant Intoxication Mountain, the King of Shattered Peaks Mountain, the King of Immortal Mountain, the King of Yoke-Bearing Mountain, the King of Horse-Ear Mountain, the King of Fish-Bearing Mountain, the King of Cakravāḍa Mountain, the King of Banner-Mark Mountain, and the King of Mount Sumeru.
O Son of the Buddha!

Just as the King of Snowy Mountains is the source from which all species of medicinal herbs emerge, and these medicinal herbs can never be exhausted by gathering, so too is it with the Bodhisattva dwelling in the Stage of Supreme Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*): he serves as the source from which all worldly scripts, treatises, prose, verse, and mantras emerge.
The various worldly treatises, arts, and crafts, as well as the prose, verses, and vidyā-mantras [taught therein], cannot be fully described.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like the great king of mountains, Gandhamādana, which is the source of all varieties of incense; among them, the various fragrances can never be exhausted when taken.

It is likewise for a bodhisattva dwelling in the Ground of Freedom from Defilement (*vimalā-bhūmi*): they serve as the source and basis for the fragrance of the conduct of the pure ethical discipline (*śīla-saṃvara*) of all bodhisattvas, because the fragrance of the conduct of the pure ethical discipline of all bodhisattvas is inexhaustible.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is, for example, like the King of Mountains, Vajraśṛṅga, which is composed entirely of pure jewels and is the source from which all varieties of precious gems emerge; therein, these various jewels can never be exhausted, no matter how much they are taken.

It is likewise for a bodhisattva dwelling in the Radiant Stage (*prabhākari-bhūmi*): they can serve as the basis and source for all mundane meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), meditative absorptions (*samādhi*), and attainments (*samāpatti*), because they are inexhaustible in answering questions regarding all mundane meditative concentrations, supernormal powers, liberations, meditative absorptions, and attainments.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like the Great Mountain King, composed entirely of precious jewels, which is the dwelling place and source of the five supernormal powers (pañcābhijñā) for divine seers; therein, the assemblies of those possessing the five supernormal powers are inexhaustible.

It is likewise for a bodhisattva dwelling in the stage of Blazing Wisdom (*arcismatī-bhūmi*): they serve as the source and basis for all superior wisdom regarding what constitutes the path and what does not; and within all inquiries and responses concerning the superior wisdom of the path and non-path, they are inexhaustible.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like the great mountain king Yugandhara, which is composed entirely of precious jewels and is the source from which all the great yakṣas emerge; therein, the hosts of all the great yakṣas are inexhaustible.

It is likewise for a bodhisattva dwelling in the Ground Difficult to Conquer (*sudurjayā*): they serve as the basis and source for all sovereign transformations of supernatural power and majesty, and are inexhaustible in their responses regarding all such sovereign transformations of supernatural power and majesty.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like the great mountain king Aśvakarṇa, which is composed entirely of precious jewels and is the source of every variety of fruit; among them, the fruits can never be exhausted, no matter how many are taken.

It is likewise for the Bodhisattva dwelling in the Stage of Presence (*sāmmukhībhūmi*): he is able to serve as the basis and source for entering into and expounding upon dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), such that his discourse on the questions and answers regarding the realization of the fruits of the Śrāvakas is inexhaustible.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like the great mountain king Mālyavat, which is composed entirely of pure jewels and is the dwelling place of all powerful nāga deities; within it, the hosts of all powerful nāgas are inexhaustible.

It is likewise for a bodhisattva dwelling in the stage of Far-Reaching (dūramgamā): they are able to expound the source from which skillful means and sublime wisdom arise, such that their explanations regarding the meaning of the questions and answers concerning the realization of the fruit of a pratyekabuddha are inexhaustible.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like the great mountain king Cakravāḍa, which is composed entirely of jewels and serves as the source and dwelling place for all the classes of sovereign beings; for these sovereign beings are inexhaustible.

It is likewise with a bodhisattva dwelling in the Immovable Stage (*acalā-bhūmi*): they are able to serve as the source and basis for eliciting all the sovereign questions and answers of bodhisattvas, such that their analytical responses to inquiries throughout all worlds are inexhaustible.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like the great mountain king Dhvajāgra, composed entirely of precious jewels, which is the source and dwelling place for the hosts of asuras of great majesty and power, for those hosts of asuras of great majesty and power are inexhaustible.

It is likewise for a bodhisattva dwelling in the stage of Good Intelligence (*sādhumatī*): they serve as the source from which the wisdom-practice that brings to rest the flow of all worldly existence emerges, and they are inexhaustible within the arising of questions and answers concerning all worlds.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is like Mount Sumeru, the king of great mountains, which is composed entirely of precious jewels and is the source and abode of the gods of great majesty; therein, the hosts of gods of great majesty are inexhaustible.
