It is likewise for a Bodhisattva dwelling in the stage of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā bhūmi*): they can serve as the source from which the powers (*bala*), the fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), and the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) emerge, manifesting inquiries and answers regarding the works of the Buddhas without end.
O Son of the Buddha!

Just as these ten kinds of great mountain kings of jewels are all manifested within the great ocean, so too are the ten stages of the bodhisattva all manifested within the knowledge of all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna), and by means of that very knowledge of all-knowledge.
“O Son of the Buddha!
For example, the great ocean is included within the category of oceans because it possesses ten characteristics that cannot be eclipsed. What are these ten?

That is to say: because it is progressively deeper; because it does not cohabit with corpses overnight; because other waters entering it lose their names and numbers; because it has a single uniform taste; because it contains many precious jewels; because it is so deep that it is difficult to descend into; because its breadth is immeasurable; because it is the dwelling place of beings of massive bodies; because its tides do not overstep the limits they have established; and because it can receive the rain from all great clouds without ever becoming satiated.
O Son of the Buddha!
The practices of all bodhisattvas are likewise; because they cannot be eclipsed by the ten aspects of practice, they are reckoned among the Great Practices. What are these ten?
That is to say:

because in the Ground of Utmost Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), one gradually brings forth great vows; because in the Ground of Purity (*vimalā-bhūmi*), the corpses of those who violate their precepts are not allowed to remain;
because in the Ground of Radiance (*prabhākari-bhūmi*), one abandons worldly designations, names, and numbers; [and] in the Ground of Blazing...
In the stage of Wisdom (Prajñābhūmi), because there is a single flavor of indestructible pure faith in all Buddhas;
in the stage of Difficult to Conquer (Sudurjayābhūmi), because it brings forth immeasurable skillful means, supernormal powers, and worldly activities which are like many precious jewels;

in the stage of Presence (Abhimukhībhūmi), because of observing the profound principle of dependent origination; and in the stage of Far-Reaching (Dūraṅgamābhūmi), because of its vast and immeasurable sublime wisdom.
Because they have attained definitive discernment of all skillful means; because they manifest the great adornments within the Immovable Ground (*acalā-bhūmi*);
because on the Good Intelligence Ground (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*), they penetrate according to principle the profound liberation and worldly activities without ever transgressing the established limits;
and because on the Cloud of Dharma Ground (*dharmameghā-bhūmi*), they are able to receive the great clouds of the light of all Buddha-dharmas—
Because it rains without ever being satisfied.
"O Son of the Buddha!

It is like a great maṇi jewel that has been obtained after surpassing ten kinds of precious natures. A master craftsman refines it with fire until it is perfectly round and flawless, pure and free from impurities, brilliantly polished and translucent, and skillfully pierced so that it may be strung with a precious thread. When it is placed atop a high banner of vaidūrya, it radiates all manner of various lights; approved by the king, it is then able to rain down all kinds of jewels, benefiting all sentient beings according to their desires and causing their heart's wishes to be completely fulfilled."

O Son of the Buddha! You should know that the mind of *sarvajñā* (omniscience) is likewise so. When a Bodhisattva’s great mind of enlightenment transcends the ten types of noble lineages, they are then able to give rise to the qualities of *dhūta* (ascetic purification). Having distanced themselves from mere prohibitions and precepts, they are well-forged and refined; their meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), absorptions (*samādhi*), and attainments (*samāpatti*) are perfected; the aspects of the factors of the path are pure and stainless; their skillful means and supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) are brilliantly polished and transparent; and through the contemplation of dependent origination, they are skillfully and wondrously pierced. Strung together with the thread of wisdom and various skillful means, this mind is placed atop the high banner of mastery. Observing the conduct of sentient beings, it radiates the light of heard wisdom; once consecrated by the wisdom of perfect enlightenment, it is then named the "Omniscient One," capable of extensively performing the Buddha-work for the entire realm of sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!

You should know that this Dharma-door chapter, which is a sublime collection of the qualities of the wisdom of omniscience in all its aspects and which can accumulate all the practices of bodhisattvas, shall never be heard by those sentient beings who have not planted roots of goodness.
The Bodhisattva Vimukticandra said: "O Son of the Buddha!

If there are sentient beings whose faculty of hearing is able to hear this chapter on the Dharma-door of the Collection of the Nature of Merit of All-Seed and All-Knowledge Wisdom, how much a mass of merit will these achieve?"
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva said:
"O Son of the Buddha!

To whatever extent there is sovereign power and majesty belonging to the knowledge of all-knowledge, because of the encompassing conditions of generating the mind of omniscience, there is likewise an accumulation of merit; and to whatever extent an accumulation of merit manifests because of the encompassing conditions of generating the mind of omniscience, one shall obtain that same accumulation of merit upon hearing this chapter on the sublime Dharma-gate."
Why is this so? Sons of the Buddha!

You should know that this Dharma-door chapter, which is a collection of the nature of the merit of the wisdom of all-knowledge, cannot be heard or believed and understood by anyone who is not a bodhisattva; how much less can they apply themselves with diligent practice through the signs of cultivation within it?
O Son of the Buddha!

Therefore, you should know that if there are sentient beings who listen to this chapter of the Dharma-door with a single-minded focus, and having heard it, believe and understand it; having understood it, receive and uphold it; and apply themselves to its practice through the signs of cultivation—all such sentient beings will accordingly follow the gateway to omniscience.

At that time, through the Buddha’s spiritual power and by the very nature of phenomena, worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten koṭis of Buddha-fields in the ten directions all shook in six ways and eighteen manners, namely:

It shook, shook everywhere, and shook equally everywhere; it rose, rose everywhere, and rose equally everywhere; it leaped, leaped everywhere, and leaped equally everywhere; it quaked, quaked everywhere, and quaked equally everywhere; it roared, roared everywhere, and roared equally everywhere; it crashed, crashed everywhere, and crashed equally everywhere. Through the spiritual power of the Buddha and by the natural law of things, clouds of celestial flowers rained down, clouds of celestial garlands, clouds of exquisite celestial garments, clouds of various celestial jewels, clouds of celestial ornaments, clouds of celestial jewel-canopies, clouds of celestial jewel-banners, and clouds of celestial jewel-pennants. Clouds of celestial music rained down, their harmonious and elegant sounds resonating simultaneously, while clouds of hymns surpassing those of all other devas rained down, extolling the ground of omniscience.

Just as this Dharma was expounded in the palace of the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven within the four great continents of this world, so too did the sound of this teaching circulate universally throughout all worlds in the ten directions.

At that time, through the spiritual power of the Buddha, from beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten koṭis of buddha-fields in each of the ten directions, there came to this assembly bodhisattva hosts as numerous as the atoms in ten koṭis of buddha-fields, filling the ten directions.
Having gathered at this assembly, they all spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent! O Son of the Buddha!"
You have now skillfully elucidated this Dharma-nature of the bodhisattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
We all likewise bear the same name, Vajragarbha. Each of us resides in a world named Vajravijaya, and the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas therein all likewise bear the same name, Vajradhvaja.

Each of us has come from those respective places; in all those worlds, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, this very Dharma is being taught, with assemblies exactly equal to ours, and with the words, phrases, and meanings identical to what is being spoken here, without any increase or decrease.
O Son of the Buddha!
We have now come to this assembly by virtue of the Buddha’s spiritual power to bear witness for you.

Just as we have entered this world, so too do we go to bear witness in every single one of all the worlds throughout the ten directions; in each of those worlds, within the four great continents, specifically in the palaces of the Sovereign Heavenly Kings of the Heaven of Making Use of Others’ Transformations, within the Maṇi-jewel Treasury Halls, we all proceed in this same manner to bear witness.

At that time, Vajragarbha Bodhisattva surveyed the entire assembly in the ten directions, illuminating the entire Dharma-realm. Desiring to praise the arousal of the bodhicitta, desiring to manifest the realm of the bodhisattvas, desiring to purify the power of the bodhisattva practices, desiring to explain the path for gathering all-knowledge, desiring to remove the defilements of all worlds, desiring to bestow the knowledge of all modes, desiring to manifest the inconceivable adornment of wisdom, and desiring to reveal the supreme merits of all bodhisattvas, he further sought to clarify and expand upon the meaning of these aforementioned stages.
Empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, he spoke in verse: “His mind is quiescent and ever-disciplined, Equanimous and unimpeded like space;”
Free from all defilements and abiding in the Way, you should listen to this sublime practice.
Having cultivated all manner of virtues for hundreds of billions of kalpas, And having made offerings to immeasurable and boundless Buddhas;
The śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas do likewise, As they give rise to the Great Mind for the benefit of all living beings.
Diligently upholding pure precepts and always being harmonious and patient, they are fully endowed with shame, remorse, merit, and wisdom;
aspiring to seek the Buddha’s wisdom and cultivating vast insight, they resolve their great minds to attain the Ten Powers.
Making offerings to all Buddhas of the three periods of time, Thoroughly purifying all lands throughout every realm;
Fully realizing that all phenomena are equal, One gives rise to the Great Mind for the benefit of sentient beings.
Having first resolved upon bodhicitta on the first bhūmi, Forever free from all evils, one is ever joyful;
Through the power of vows, one extensively cultivates all wholesome dharmas, And out of compassion, enters the subsequent stages.
Fully endowed with precepts and meditative concentration, one keeps sentient beings in mind; having washed away defilements, the mind is bright and pure.
Observing that the fires of the three poisons blaze within the world, the one of vast understanding proceeds to the third stage.
All that exists within the three realms is impermanent, Like an arrow piercing the body, there is no refuge;
Disgusted with the conditioned, he seeks the Buddha-dharma, And with vast wisdom, proceeds toward the stage of Blazing Wisdom.
Endowed with mindfulness and wisdom, they attain the knowledge of the Path; They make offerings to hundreds of thousands of immeasurable Buddhas;
Constantly contemplating the most supreme merits— This is the entry into the Difficult-to-Conquer Stage (Sudurjayā).
Skillfully observing with wisdom and skillful means, manifesting various forms to save sentient beings;
furthermore, making offerings to the Unsurpassed Honored One of Ten Powers—this is the way to enter the Ground of Presence.
That which is difficult for the world to know, he knows; unattached to a self, he is free from existence and non-existence.
The nature of phenomena is fundamentally quiescent yet turns according to conditions; by means of this wondrous wisdom, he advances toward the seventh stage.
With wisdom, skillful means, and a vast mind, Difficult to practice, difficult to subdue, and difficult to comprehend;
Though having realized quiescence, they diligently cultivate, Able to attain the Immovable Ground, as vast as space.
Having received the Buddha’s exhortation to arise from quiescent extinction, They extensively cultivate the various karmas of wisdom;
Possessing the ten masteries, they contemplate the world, And by this means ascend to the Stage of Excellent Intelligence.
With subtle and wondrous wisdom, he observes sentient beings—the dense forests of mind, afflictions, karma, and the like;
desiring to transform them so they may enter the Path, he expounds the supreme treasury of the Buddhas’ ultimate meaning.
Practicing the stages in succession and perfecting all virtues, Accumulating merit and wisdom through the nine stages;
Constantly seeking the most supreme Dharma of all Buddhas, One receives the empowerment with the water of Buddha-wisdom.
He attained countless samādhis, thoroughly understanding their respective functions;
subsequently, he entered the samādhi named "Receiving Empowerment," abiding unwaveringly within the vast objective realm.
When the Bodhisattva attains this subsequent concentration, a great precious lotus suddenly appears;
his body, proportionate in size, sits within it, surrounded by a multitude of Bodhisattvas who gaze upon him together.
He emits hundreds of billions of great rays of light, Which extinguish the suffering of all sentient beings;
Again, from the crown of his head he emits light, Which enters universally into the assemblies of the Buddhas of the ten directions;
It abides entirely in the air, forming a net of light, And having made offerings to the Buddhas, it enters through their feet.
At that moment, all the Buddhas knew this: that the Son of the Buddha had now ascended to the stage of consecration (*abhiṣeka*).
Bodhisattvas from the ten directions all gathered there; beholding this Great Being, they attained various meditative concentrations.
The Buddhas also emitted light from between their eyebrows, which shone everywhere and entered through the crown of his head.
The worlds of the ten directions all tremble, and the sufferings of all evil realms are extinguished;
at that time, the Buddhas anoint his crown, just as a Wheel-Turning King anoints his crown prince.
If one receives the empowerment conferred by all Buddhas, this is called ascending to the Stage of the Dharma-Cloud;
with wisdom increasing boundlessly, one brings awakening to all worlds.
The realm of desire, the realm of form, and the formless realm; the realm of phenomena, the world-realm, and the realm of sentient beings;
the conditioned, the unconditioned, and empty nirvana—all such things he thoroughly penetrates.
All transformations and great powers, the subtle wisdom sustained by the Buddhas,
the secret kalpas and the paths of the pores— all these they are able to observe as they truly are.
Taking birth, renouncing the world, and attaining perfect enlightenment; turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma and entering nirvana;
even up to the dharma of tranquil liberation—all that is taught and explained, they are able to comprehend.
When Bodhisattvas dwell in this stage of the Cloud of Dharma, they are fully endowed with the power of mindfulness to uphold the Buddha-dharma;
just as the great ocean receives the rain from the dragons, so too does this stage receive the Dharma.
Even if all sentient beings throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions, as numerous as motes of dust,
were each to attain the dhāraṇī of hearing and retaining, and each were to uphold various and immeasurable teachings;

When a Bodhisattva dwells in this Stage of the Cloud of Dharma, the teachings received from a single Buddha are called the "Treasury of the Dharma-realm of the Three Times"; they exceed those [from all others] and are immeasurable.
By the majestic power of his ancient wisdom-vows, he pervades the worlds of the ten directions in a single thought;
by pouring down the nectar of the Dharma, he extinguishes afflictions—therefore, this stage is named "Dharma Cloud."
The manifestations of supernormal powers pervade the ten directions, transcending the realms of humans, devas, and the mundane world;
even exceeding these by immeasurable billions, they would surely cause confusion if one were to contemplate them with worldly wisdom.
The physical actions and so forth of a Bodhisattva on the tenth stage, up to the measure of wisdom required for lifting a foot—
these are the qualities of one who has ascended to the rank of the Dharma Prince; they cannot be fathomed by the noble ones of the ninth stage,
much less by all sentient beings, nor by Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
The Bodhisattvas of this stage make offerings to the Buddhas, pervading all lands throughout the ten directions;
they also make offerings to the assembly of noble ones present before them, fully adorning the merits of the Buddhas.

The Buddhas teach this for those who dwell on this stage: the unimpeded wisdom regarding the dharma-realm of the three times, which universally illumines all sentient beings throughout the worlds, and even teaches them the knowledge of all modes.
The light of wisdom of the Bodhisattvas on this stage can show sentient beings the path of the True Dharma;
like the light of the Great Lord Śakra, it dispels darkness and gladdens the bodies of sentient beings.
The light of wisdom on this stage likewise dispels darkness and brings joy to the world.
Dwelling here, they mostly act as kings of the three realms, skillfully expounding the Dharma of the three vehicles;
in a single kṣaṇa, they can realize hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of unspeakable numbers.
The samādhis equal to the atoms of the buddha-fields, and the seeing of Buddhas and other such matters are likewise;
I have now briefly explained this stage, for it could not be fully described even if one were to speak at length.
These stages stand majestically within the Buddha’s wisdom like the ten mountain kings;
the arts and learning of the first stage are inexhaustible, like the medicinal properties in the Snowy Mountains;
the fragrance of the precepts in the second stage is like the Fragrant Mountain.
The third is like the vast and wondrous treasures of a wealthy man;
the Jewel Path of Blazing Wisdom is inexhaustible, like the multitude of divine immortals in the mountains of the seers;
the fifth stage of supernatural powers is like the mountain of Dhrūtarāṣṭra.
Sixth, like the horse-ear [continent], it possesses all fruits;
seventh, the great wisdom of the stage of the earth is like holding a fish;
eighth, mastery is like the Cakravāḍa mountain range.
The nine unhindered analytical knowledges are like the banner-sign;
the tenth is like Mount Sumeru, possessing all virtues.
In the first stage, vows are foremost; in the second, pure ethical discipline; in the third, meditative concentration and other such merits.
The fourth is the path of the awakening factor of one-pointed application; The fifth is the subtle skillful means and wisdom of the ground;
The sixth is the profound contemplation of dependent origination; The seventh is vast wisdom and the eighth is adornment;
The ninth is the discernment of subtle meanings, A path that transcends all worlds.
On the tenth stage, one upholds all the Buddha-dharmas; such an ocean of practice is inexhaustible. The ten practices transcend the world:
the first is the initial generation of the mind; the second is pure morality; the third is meditative concentration;
the fourth is the purity of conduct; the fifth is accomplishment; the sixth is dependent origination; and the seventh is penetration.
The eighth is established upon the Vajradhvaja; the ninth observes the dense forest of sentient beings;
the tenth is the Dharma King conferring empowerment—thus do these jewels of virtue gradually become purified.
The lands of the ten directions may be ground into dust, and their number known in a single thought;
the space traversed by a single hair-tip may be measured, yet to speak of this for billions of eons would never reach its end.
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajragarbha had spoken this sutra through the Buddha’s spiritual power, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha praised and confirmed it.

All those great assemblies of bodhisattvas, as well as the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, Śakra, Brahmā, the world-protectors, Maheśvara, and the hosts of Śuddhāvāsa devas, were all greatly delighted; they received it with faith and practiced accordingly.

At that time, not long after the Blessed One had attained enlightenment, on the second seventh-day period, he was in the Maṇiratnanidhi Hall in the palace of the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, rejoicing in what the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha had spoken.

The Tenth Stage, the Cloud of Dharma, of the Bodhisattva is completed. The Ninth Scroll of the *Daśabhūmika Sūtra*. With exquisite dancing, music, jesting, laughter, and conversation, they joyfully advance together in the supreme practice of the Path.
